why: A concatenation without the variable itself among its elements keeps its class `C` when at least one element holds a `C` and no element is known to hold an object of another class (step 15 round 7b ruling). MATLAB R2026a gives one of three: an array of `C`, the class's own `horzcat` run (project rule: it gives the object back), or an error (`[k, 5]`, `[5, k]` and `[k, w]` with `w` of another class, measured for a classdef and an old-style class), past which no later call is reached. So `k = [a, 5]` with `a` a `Gizmo` keeps `tidy(k)` the class's, as its transpose does; `[a, b]` with `b` a `Widget` holds two known classes and gives none, so `tidy(k)` is the plain `tidy`; so does `[[a, b], a]`, an element that holds two, and `[a, zpk.Wdg()]`, a package's class constructed; so is `[]'`, an empty double, and `[5, 6]'`, no object at all.
